question_text:
What happens when light falls on a mirror? 
(जब दर्पण पर प्रकाश पड़ता है तो क्या होता है?)
options: It passes through it. (यह इसके पार चला जाता है।)
It gets absorbed. (यह अवशोषित हो जाता है।)
It gets reflected. (यह परावर्तित हो जाता है।)
It gets scattered in all directions. (यह सभी दिशाओं में बिखर जाता है।)
answer: It gets reflected. (यह परावर्तित हो जाता है।)
explanation: A mirror is a polished and smooth surface that bounces back most of the light falling on it in a predictable manner, known as reflection. (दर्पण एक पॉलिश की हुई और चिकनी सतह होती है जो उस पर पड़ने वाले अधिकांश प्रकाश को वापस मोड़ देती है, जिसे परावर्तन कहा जाता है।)
distractor_rationale: Mirrors are opaque, so light cannot pass through. They are shiny, so they don't absorb much light. A mirror is smooth, so it reflects regularly, not scattering it randomly.

ai_context.learning_goal: Understand the basic function of a mirror with respect to light.
common_misconceptions: Mirrors absorb light and hold the image inside.
ai_context.hint: Think about what a mirror does to your face's image. Does the light go behind the mirror, or does it come back to you?

question_text:
If the angle of incidence is 30°, what will be the angle of reflection? 
(यदि आपतन कोण 30° है, तो परावर्तन कोण क्या होगा?)
explanation: According to the first law of reflection, the angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection (∠i = ∠r). (परावर्तन के पहले नियम के अनुसार, आपतन कोण हमेशा परावर्तन कोण के बराबर होता है (∠i = ∠r)।)
distractor_rationale: 15° is half, 60° is double (or angle with mirror surface), 90° is perpendicular. Only 30° satisfies the law ∠i = ∠r.

ai_context.learning_goal: Apply the first law of reflection mathematically.
common_misconceptions: Angle of reflection depends on the medium or the type of light.
Angle of reflection is the angle between the ray and the mirror, not the normal.
ai_context.hint: Recall the Law of Reflection: The incoming angle and the bouncing angle (measured from the normal) are always identical.

question_text:
Which instrument uses multiple reflections to create beautiful patterns? 
(कौन सा उपकरण सुंदर पैटर्न बनाने के लिए बहु-परावर्तन का उपयोग करता है?)
explanation: A kaleidoscope contains multiple mirrors placed at angles to each other. Glass pieces inside form multiple reflections, creating endless unique patterns. (कैलिडोस्कोप में एक-दूसरे के कोण पर रखे कई दर्पण होते हैं। अंदर कांच के टुकड़े कई परावर्तन बनाते हैं, जिससे अनगिनत अद्वितीय पैटर्न बनते हैं।)
distractor_rationale: Microscopes and Telescopes use lenses/mirrors to magnify. Periscopes use multiple reflection but to see over obstacles, not to create beautiful patterns. Only kaleidoscopes are designed for patterns.

ai_context.learning_goal: Identify practical applications of multiple reflections.
ai_context.hint: It's a toy you look into, and as you turn it, broken bangles create new symmetrical designs.

question_text:
Which part of the human eye controls the amount of light entering it? 
(मानव आँख का कौन सा भाग उसमें प्रवेश करने वाले प्रकाश की मात्रा को नियंत्रित करता है?)
explanation: The iris acts like a shutter. It adjusts the size of the pupil to control how much light enters the eye. (परितारिका एक शटर की तरह काम करती है। यह पुतली के आकार को समायोजित करती है ताकि यह नियंत्रित किया जा सके कि आंख में कितना प्रकाश प्रवेश करता है।)
distractor_rationale: Cornea is the clear front window. Retina is the screen where image forms. Optic nerve carries signals to brain. The Iris is the only structure that expands and contracts.

ai_context.learning_goal: Identify the function of the Iris in the human eye.
common_misconceptions: The pupil is a solid object that grows and shrinks.
ai_context.hint: It's the colored part of your eye that opens up wider in the dark.

question_text:
Why can we read words printed on a piece of paper but cannot see our face on it? 
(हम कागज के एक टुकड़े पर छपे शब्दों को क्यों पढ़ सकते हैं लेकिन उस पर अपना चेहरा क्यों नहीं देख सकते हैं?)
options: Paper absorbs all light. (कागज सभी प्रकाश को अवशोषित कर लेता है।)
Paper causes regular reflection. (कागज नियमित परावर्तन का कारण बनता है।)
Paper causes diffused (irregular) reflection. (कागज विसरित (अनियमित) परावर्तन का कारण बनता है।)
Paper produces its own light. (कागज अपना प्रकाश स्वयं उत्पन्न करता है।)
answer: Paper causes diffused (irregular) reflection. (कागज विसरित (अनियमित) परावर्तन का कारण बनता है।)
explanation: A piece of paper is a rough surface microscopically. Parallel light rays falling on it are reflected in different directions (diffused reflection), which scatters the light rather than forming an image. (कागज का एक टुकड़ा सूक्ष्म रूप से एक खुरदरी सतह है। इस पर पड़ने वाली समानांतर प्रकाश किरणें विभिन्न दिशाओं में परावर्तित होती हैं (विसरित परावर्तन), जो एक छवि बनाने के बजाय प्रकाश को बिखेर देती हैं।)
distractor_rationale: If paper absorbed all light, it would look completely black. If it caused regular reflection, it would act like a mirror. Paper is non-luminous, so it doesn't produce light.

ai_context.learning_goal: Differentiate between regular and diffused reflection based on surface smoothness.
common_misconceptions: Diffused reflection means the laws of reflection have failed.
Paper doesn't reflect light at all.
ai_context.hint: Think about the microscopic surface of paper compared to glass. It's bumpy, so light rays bounce off in all random directions!
